author: ojiudezue
title: Music following's MA-first path has never run in a WiiM room: it matches a dead Music Assistant twin
summary: A read-only probe for step 8 found that in all 10 WiiM rooms music following's _ma_candidates picks the _5 Music Assistant twin, which is unavailable in every recorder row for 7 days, while the _7 twin that actually plays (identifier wiim_uuid:<uuid>) never matches any rule. Every transfer falls back to native WiiM join, so music still follows, but the v5.108.26 MA-first repair has never executed there. The same probe found no MA queue started in a week, so the arrival engine's 'is this our music' marker cannot be learned from history; the engine ships nothing until that is settled live or by a context-based ownership rule.
why: The v5.108.26 D0 inventory matched twins by MAC-in-identifier and stopped at 'a twin exists'; it never checked the twin's state or which entity was actually playing. A fire check (has the MA path ever run?) would have caught it at ship. The fallback hid the failure because the user-visible behaviour still worked.
alternatives_considered: Delete the stale _5 players in Music Assistant (operator-side; leaves URA matching fragile for the next provider change)
Leave native join as the only path (gives up MA queue transfer, which the arrival engine needs)
implications: Twin resolution must prefer an available entity and match the wiim_uuid identifier from the registry. Any feature with a fallback path needs a fire check on the primary path, or the fallback silently becomes the product.
revisit_trigger: Music Assistant provider changes, or MF digest shows ma_source_not_playing after the fix.
